newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals plan C$1.8 bln in spending.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals plan C$1.8 bln in spending.

text.p: Canada's governing Liberals want to spend almost C$2 billion by the spring of the year 2000 if they win the June 2 election, the opposition Reform party charged on Tuesday.
A Reform party spokeswoman said the party had obtained a copy of the Liberal election platform which outlined spending of C$1.8 billion by March 2000.

"It really is going to cost Canadians more money, this whole plan," party spokeswoman Carolyn Stewart Olsen said in a phone interview from the party headquarters in Calgary. "There's nothing in here that addresses the issues most troubling Canadians today."

She said the spending outlined in the platform document did not include the cancellation of C$7 billion in health care cuts announced by the Liberals as they launched their election campaign earlier this week.
A Liberal party spokesman confirmed that the Reform party had obtained the document, but he would not comment on its contents.

"We're going to be releasing the platform officially tomorrow in Saskatoon," the spokesman said in a phone interview from Ottawa. The party had originally scheduled the release of the document for Thursday in Ottawa, he said.
"We're not really getting into the numbers tonight," he said. "It's a balanced approach to governing."

The Liberals, who have governed Canada for the past 3 1/2 years, have been campaigning since the election was called last Sunday on their record of fixing Canada's economic problems and drastically reducing the deficit. Now that Canada's economy is on the mend, the government can afford to reinvest in social programs, the party says.

Earlier on Tuesday, Finance Minister Paul Martin said the cancellation of the C$7 billion in health care cuts would be the biggest spending item on the Liberals' list of election goodies. ((Heather Scoffield, Reuters Ottawa Bureau 613-235-6745))
